name: O-Town
notes: An American manufactured boy band working a UK-produced ballad template, and the research states the ballad feel explicitly — 64–92 with a "6/8-ish subdivision with the backbeat on 3" — so `halfTime` is true and the snare is `halftime_3`. The stated 100–124 uptempo band is the other backbeat class and is named here rather than encoded, because one session block carries one backbeat. The harmony is fully documented: C major throughout with a modulation to D after the bridge, I–vi–IV–V under the verse and IV–V–I on the chorus lift. Three drum facts are authored — "kick 1 and 3", "snare (often a brushed or gated sample) on 3 in the slow songs", and "16th hat only from chorus 2", which is why the hat base is 8th-weighted with a low fill density, plus the "tom fill into the modulation" as a tom lane and a wide fill schedule. The group range G3–A4 is tight "so the five voices can stack", and the chorus is "a 4-note descending cell repeated with harmony added each time", which is the narrow register with a descend-heavy contour and a two-bar phrase. ⚠ `confidence` is medium because the research rates it high-medium. ⚠ The **INFERRED** parameters are all drum probabilities and `bpm.mode` 78. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than the held `reese_sustain` the research describes** — *“keyboard bass on roots, whole- or half-note durations under the ballads; played bass on the uptempos.”* — and that is a limit of the engine rather than a reading of the record. `generators::phrase_spans` re-articulates a held span only when it runs longer than two bars, so over the four-bar clip `reese_sustain` writes at most four notes and cannot reach the 500-bassline floor `engine/tests/bass.rs` holds every model to. `mobb-deep`, `dmx` and `capone-n-noreaga` carry the same substitution for the same reason; `followRootsProb` stays where it was so the line still reads as roots under the chord. ⚠ **The bassline reached 921 of 1,000 distinct against `bass.rs`'s 0.95 share.** The research names two low ends, and only the first was authored: *"keyboard bass on roots, whole- or half-note durations under the ballads; **played bass on the uptempos**"*. A played bass is the half that moves, and `followRootsProb` 0.92 with an `M2` beside `P5` is where it lives in one blended model. ⚠ **INFERRED:** the exact 0.92, the `M2` and `anticipationProb` 0.20 are lane-conventional rates, not sourced ones.
